checks.sources_say: Customer email states 'Policy number: VER-1004'; the repair quote header states 'Insurer: Veridia Insurance, policy VER-1004'; Policy Schedule policy_id is VER-1004 for holder Thomas Petit.
checks.evidence: Customer email (2026-10-28) signature block; repair_quote.pdf customer block; Policy Schedule VER-1004

checks.sources_say: The Policy Schedule for VER-1004 lists coverages C1 (Third-party liability) and C2 (Collision damage). The email describes the policyholder hitting a post in a car park, damaging his own vehicle — damage to the insured vehicle after a collision, which is C2 per contract Article 2. C2 is in the Policy Schedule, so Article 2/7 referral for unlisted coverage does not apply.
checks.evidence: Policy Schedule coverages list; customer email incident description; contract.pdf Article 2 (document 2630#10414, page 1)

checks.sources_say: Email: 'I hit a post in an underground car park on 27 October 2026.'
Email received on 2026-10-28 (header date), one day after the incident; contract Article 4.1 requires reporting within 5 calendar days of the incident, so the claim is within the deadline.
checks.evidence: Customer email header 'received on 2026-10-28'; contract.pdf Article 4.1 (document 2630#10414, page 2)

checks.sources_say: repair_quote.pdf (Garage Central Auto, quote Q-2610-5283, issued 28/10/2026) shows TOTAL INCL. VAT = 1 640,00 €. Contract Article 1 defines repair cost as the total amount including VAT on the repair quote. The phone estimate of 'around €900' in the email is superseded by the written quote, which is the governing document.
checks.evidence: repair_quote.pdf totals table ('TOTAL INCL. VAT 1 640,00 €'); contract.pdf Article 1 definition of Repair cost (document 2630#10414, page 1)

checks.sources_say: Email: 'I hit a post in an underground car park... Nobody else was involved' — the policyholder caused the damage to his own vehicle, so he is at fault. This also means the Article 5.2 not-at-fault waiver (no deductible when not at fault AND third party identified) does not apply, consistent with the €300 C2 standard deductible.
checks.evidence: Customer email body; contract.pdf Article 5.2 and Article 2 C2 standard deductible €300 (document 2630#10414, pages 1-2)

checks.sources_say: Email: 'Nobody else was involved.' No other driver or vehicle is mentioned anywhere in the email or the quote.

With no third party involved, there is no third party to identify; recording false is consistent. The handler playbook rule on referring claims involving a commercial other driver (van, truck, lorry, delivery vehicle) is not triggered, because the email states nobody else was involved.
checks.evidence: Customer email ('Nobody else was involved'); handler playbook as given in the review request

checks.sources_say: The email attaches repair_quote.pdf and damage_photos.zip. repair_quote.pdf names customer Thomas Petit, vehicle Volkswagen Golf (2020), policy VER-1004 — it belongs to this policyholder and vehicle. damage_photos.zip is stored by the mailroom and counted as received. For C2, contract Article 4 requires photos of the damage and a repair quote (an accident report signed by both drivers is required only when a third party is involved, which is not the case here). Both required documents are provided.
checks.evidence: Customer email attachment list; repair_quote.pdf customer/vehicle/policy block; contract.pdf Article 4 required-documents table for C2 (document 2630#10414, page 2)

checks.sources_say: Nothing in the email or the quote indicates any Article 3 exclusion: no alcohol/drugs, the policyholder holds a valid licence since 2008-11-01 (Policy Schedule), no racing/track use, no intentional damage, and the damage is collision damage from hitting a post, not wear or mechanical failure. No exclusion signal is correct, so Article 7.2 referral does not apply.
checks.evidence: Customer email and repair_quote.pdf (no exclusion indicators); contract.pdf Article 3 exclusions (document 2630#10414, page 2); Policy Schedule licence_date 2008-11-01

verdict.summary: All recorded facts match the customer email, the repair quote (total incl. VAT €1,640 per Article 1), and the Policy Schedule; the claim was reported within 5 days, C2 coverage applies, required documents were provided, no exclusion or playbook referral rule is triggered, so the staged payment can be approved.
